title: State-visit distribution moments (skewness · excess kurtosis) on n=4 ECA
question: Do life-class rules show ≥1.5× higher excess kurtosis (heavier tails) than consciousness-class rules on the 100-step state-visit histogram?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=4 ECA ring, 16 starts × 100 steps = 1600 visits per rule, 16-bin histogram. Pearson moments (excess kurtosis = μ₄/σ⁴ − 3).

falsifier_eval.F330_1_KURT_LIFE_GT_CONSC_BY_1_5x: FAIL — ratio 1.05× far below 1.5×; life and consc kurtoses overlap in [-1.36, -1.19] band
falsifier_eval.F330_2_BIJECTION_DISCOVERY: PASS-WITH-FINDING — rule_105/150/204 ALL collapse to identical {mean 7.5, var 21.25, skew 0.0, kurt -1.209} = perfectly uniform-on-visited 16-state. This is the *bijection signature*: every state visits every other state exactly once over the orbit, regardless of being labelled life-class or consc-class or identity. The bijection class is structural, not life/consc-conceptual.
falsifier_eval.F330_3_ANCHOR_NON_TRIVIAL: PASS — rule_0 null collapses to single-state attractor giving skew 13, kurt 180 (extreme), distinct from all live rules; non-tautological

verdict_derived: 🔴 FALSIFIED — H1 (kurtosis discriminates life vs consc) is decisively false. The true structural axis the data exposes is BIJECTION (rules whose orbit visits all 16 states uniformly) vs NON-BIJECTION — rule_105/150 (consc) AND rule_204 (identity) all bijection; rule_30/110 (life) non-bijection. This re-confirms H_329's bonus discovery (descriptor C bijection-blind) from a completely independent moments-based angle. Three consecutive cells (H_325 Gini / H_329 unique_states / H_330 moments) converge on: bijection vs chaotic is the real axis, not life vs consc.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel (forward orbit histogram) yet 🔴 — same scale-conditional pattern as H_327. The new layer of finding is that consciousness-themed rules happen to be in the bijection class, which is dynamically *more uniform* than life-themed (chaotic) rules — flipping the naive 'consciousness = rich/complex' intuition again.
honest_limits: n=4 panel; bijection class is small (4 of 256 rules) and over-represented in the consc tag
Mean of 2 rules per class; broader Cifar-style panel would harden the verdict
Excess kurtosis below -1.2 is the platykurtic floor for 16-bin uniform — kurtosis is saturating not discriminating; higher-moment / KL-divergence-from-uniform may be more informative
100 steps × 16 starts = enough to saturate, but transient bias could survive on rule_30 — burn-in then measure would clean this up
